prompts.prompt: Reviewers bounced docs/adr/0007-auth.md (Cognito replacing our home-grown auth). Rewrite it in place so it survives the next review, using the real numbers in notes.md. The decision itself (Cognito) stays. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state it in the file.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's specific bar (one-sentence active decision with a reason, steelmanned alternatives, Good/Bad/Neutral consequences with baselines, Status, no vague quantifiers, AWS claims sourced or flagged) turns the notes into a record that holds up. Without it, models tend to keep a straw-man tone toward Auth0 and drop Neutral consequences and baselines.

floor_checks.text: The ADR still exists, names Cognito, and has a Status line
floor_checks.check: test -f docs/adr/0007-auth.md && grep -qi cognito docs/adr/0007-auth.md && grep -qiE 'status' docs/adr/0007-auth.md

rubric.criterion: Straw-man alternatives are replaced with fair ones from notes.md
rubric.pass: Auth0 gets its real strengths (rules engine, hosted login, SOC 2 Type II) and is rejected on cost ($12,600 vs ~$8,250/month); home-grown gets zero license cost and team familiarity (4 of 6) and is rejected on SLA misses and incidents
rubric.partial: Strengths listed for one alternative but not the other, or rejection reasons not evidence-based
rubric.fail: Auth0 still framed as insecure or home-grown as a 'terrible idea'

rubric.criterion: Decision and consequences follow the skill's format
rubric.pass: One active-voice sentence 'We will use Cognito because ...' citing p99 310 ms vs 1,450 ms against the 500 ms SLA; consequences split Good/Bad/Neutral with specifics (2 of 6 know Cognito, ~3 week dual-write, runbook/dashboard changes)
rubric.partial: Decision sentence present but without a concrete reason, or Neutral consequences missing
rubric.fail: Decision still passive or buried; consequences still 'will significantly improve performance'

rubric.criterion: Context states the problem with data and why now
rubric.pass: Context cites 1,450 ms p99 over 30 days vs 500 ms SLA, 3 Q2 2025 incidents and 12 dependent teams, with no judgement about the winner
rubric.partial: Some data, but vague words remain ('often slow') or context argues for Cognito
rubric.fail: Context is still 'recently many teams have concerns'

rubric.criterion: No invented numbers or links; AWS claims are sourced to notes.md or flagged for validation
rubric.pass: Every number appears in notes.md; Cognito cost/performance claims are attributed to the staging test/notes or marked to verify; no fabricated URLs
rubric.partial: One unsourced number or a placeholder link presented as real
rubric.fail: Several invented figures, benchmarks or links

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: fairness to Auth0 and the home-grown option
whether the decision sentence carries a measured reason

prompts.prompt: Write the decision record for using gRPC instead of REST for internal service-to-service calls and save it as docs/decisions/0002-internal-rpc.md. Facts: 9 internal services; p99 latency for the order->inventory call dropped from 38 ms (REST/JSON) to 12 ms (gRPC) in a 7-day staging trial (dashboard 'rpc-latency'); 4 of 9 teams already use protobuf; browser clients still need REST through the existing API gateway; we also considered Thrift and keeping REST with HTTP/2 + keep-alive (that got p99 to 27 ms). Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state it in the file.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill demands fair alternatives (REST+HTTP/2 is a genuine contender at 27 ms), baselines with measurement windows, Neutral consequences, and no invented evidence. Thrift has no data in the prompt, so a strong record describes it fairly without fabricating numbers; a weaker one invents a benchmark or dismisses it.

floor_checks.text: The record exists and states the decision with 'We will'

rubric.criterion: REST with HTTP/2 is treated as a real alternative
rubric.pass: States its real strengths (no new IDL/tooling, 27 ms is already a 29% cut from 38 ms, browser path unchanged) and rejects it on the measured 27 ms vs 12 ms gap
rubric.partial: Mentioned with the 27 ms number but no strengths
rubric.fail: Dismissed as obviously inferior or omitted

rubric.criterion: Format per the skill: Status, one-sentence decision with reason, alternatives table with a why-not-chosen column, Good/Bad/Neutral consequences
rubric.pass: All present; consequences specific (5 of 9 teams adopt protobuf; gateway keeps REST for browsers; CI codegen step as Neutral)
rubric.partial: Most present but consequences generic or Neutral missing

rubric.pass: Thrift described without invented benchmarks (or marked untested); 'rpc-latency' cited by name, no made-up URL; baseline and 7-day window stated
rubric.fail: Multiple invented numbers, studies or links

rubric.criterion: The browser/REST coexistence constraint is carried into consequences
rubric.pass: Explains that the API gateway keeps REST for browsers, so two protocols are supported and someone owns the translation layer
rubric.partial: Mentions browsers need REST without consequences

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: fair treatment of REST+HTTP/2 and Thrift

prompts.prompt: We're replacing the hamburger menu in our iOS/Android app with a bottom tab bar (Home, Orders, Search, Account). Write the UX decision record to docs/decisions/ux-0003-nav.md. Usability study: 14 participants; 11 found 'order history' faster with the tab bar (median 6 s vs 14 s). Designs are in the Figma file 'Nav v3'. Our PM wants it to say the change will 'significantly boost engagement'. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state it in the file.
prompts.why_discriminating: The UXDR guidance asks for research cited with participant counts, mockup references, accessibility (WCAG) and cross-platform implications, and the plain-writing rules reject unsupported vague quantifiers. A strong answer converts the PM's claim into a measurable target or marks it unmeasured instead of repeating it.

floor_checks.text: The record exists and cites the study size
floor_checks.check: test -f docs/decisions/ux-0003-nav.md && grep -q 14 docs/decisions/ux-0003-nav.md && grep -q 11 docs/decisions/ux-0003-nav.md

rubric.criterion: The PM's 'significantly boost engagement' claim is handled honestly
rubric.pass: Replaced with a measurable target and baseline to track (e.g. weekly Orders-tab visits) or explicitly marked as not yet measured
rubric.partial: Softened but still an unsupported claim
rubric.fail: Repeated as stated, or backed with invented numbers

rubric.pass: Cites 11 of 14 and the 6 s vs 14 s medians, references 'Nav v3', addresses accessibility with a WCAG reference (labels, touch target size, contrast) and iOS vs Android/tablet/landscape behaviour
rubric.partial: Two or three of these present
rubric.fail: Generic ADR with no accessibility or platform discussion

rubric.criterion: Alternatives are viable and consequences specific
rubric.pass: At least one real alternative (keep hamburger, hybrid) with strengths; consequences cover the 4-tab limit and where other menu items go, analytics event changes, Android back-navigation norms
rubric.partial: Alternatives present but thin, or consequences generic ('better UX')
rubric.fail: No alternatives or only straw men

rubric.criterion: One-sentence active decision and a Status
rubric.pass: 'We will replace ... with a bottom tab bar because ...' plus Status
rubric.partial: Decision present but without a reason or Status
rubric.fail: Decision not stated in one sentence

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: handling of the unsupported engagement claim
